# Alibre Script Runner

- Script Runner turns a folder of Python scripts into a menu, so you can run your Alibre automation without opening an editor each time.
  - What it does
    - Connects to a copy of Alibre Design that is already running.
    - Scans a folder you choose and turns each script it finds into a menu item.
    - Groups the menus by subfolder, and collects loose scripts under a Root Scripts menu.
    - Runs each script with the Alibre Script API already available, so your code can get straight to work.
    - Lets you point it at a different folder while it is running.
    - Shows script errors in a dialog instead of hiding them.
    - Ships sample scripts covering constraints, bolts, gears, lofts, sketches, and reference geometry.
  - What you need
    - Alibre Design installed and running with a document open.
    - Python available to run the launcher.
  - Getting started
    - Clone the repository and run `git submodule update --init --recursive`.
    - Open Alibre Design and the part you want to work on.
    - Run `source/main.py` to open the launcher.
    - Use File and then Set Base Path to point it at your own scripts folder.
  - Where things live
    - `source/` holds the runner and the sample scripts.
    - `submodules/` holds the shared example scripts.
    - `documentation/` holds reference notes.
  - Good to know
    - Scripts run against the live model, so save your work before running something new.
